summary: This bill bans companies from using automated AI systems based on surveillance data about individuals' personal information or behavior to set personalized prices for consumers or wages for workers, with narrow exceptions like cost-of-living adjustments or group discounts, and enforces the bans through FTC and EEOC actions, state attorneys general, and private lawsuits awarding up to $3,000 per violation.

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes new regulatory prohibitions on surveillance-based pricing and wage setting, enforced by FTC, EEOC, states, and private actions. It does not appropriate funds, authorize new spending, or directly affect government budgets. Enforcement uses existing agency powers under FTC Act and others. No bearing on expanding or reducing government spending.
The bill has no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection. It addresses pricing and wages via regulation, not taxation.
No mentions of healthcare, insurance, coverage, or medical services. The bill focuses on consumer pricing and worker wages using AI surveillance.
The bill does not address firearms, regulations, rights, or related issues.
No references to immigration, borders, pathways, or protections.
The bill contains no content related to abortion access or restrictions.
No provisions on military, defense spending, or related matters.
The bill does not engage with environmental protections, climate regulations, or natural resources.
Focuses on private wages and consumer prices, not government welfare, food stamps, or safety net programs.
Referred to Education and Workforce committee due to wage provisions, but no content on schools, funding, or education policy.
No relation to drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement.
Enforcement is civil via FTC, EEOC, states, and private suits with penalties and injunctions. No criminal penalties, sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
Addresses domestic commerce in pricing and wages, not international trade, tariffs, or protectionism.
No discussion of deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
Surveillance data includes personal traits, but bill is general consumer/worker protection, not specific to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No foreign policy or aid provisions.
Unrelated to voting access, elections, or integrity.

The bill primarily regulates automated decision systems (AI/tech) using surveillance data for personalized pricing and wages. Prohibits such uses, requires data accuracy processes, consumer/worker challenge rights, disclosures of data use, and invalidates arbitration clauses. This imposes significant oversight on tech companies' data practices and AI deployment, enhancing data protection and transparency against discriminatory pricing/wages. Core focus of the bill, strong push for more regulation.

Section 5 explicitly preserves collective bargaining rights over surveillance-based wage issues, sets this Act as a minimum standard, allows stronger union-negotiated protections, requires advance notice under existing CBAs, and deems union agreements enforceable. Complements general worker protections via private actions against discriminatory wage AI. Enhances worker protections and union power in AI wage context, moderate-to-strong impact as dedicated section.
No references to religion, exemptions, or anti-discrimination beyond general personal data in surveillance (not targeted at religious issues).
